description: Hard multi-hop tasks for the variant matrix (issue #125): transitive callers, blast radius, call-chain flows, same-name symbols and tests that reach a function. Gold sets were computed by evals/agent/groundtruth/hard_tasks.py from call graphs built with compiler tooling (Go: go/packages + SSA via gotool edges, three GOOS; TypeScript: the type checker via ts_edges.js; Python: import-aware AST resolution via py_edges.py, cross-checked against grep), never from myceliums output. Each gold item lists one evidence line (a call site on the chain or the definition of an end point) that check-tasks re-verifies; its note gives the level or the next hop.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods call `Pattern.MatchItem` (src/pattern.go) directly, call such a caller, or call one of those - that is, every caller up to three levels up the call chain? Count only direct calls of named functions and methods: a call made inside a closure or function literal counts for the named function that contains it; calls through interface values or function variables do not count. Include platform-specific files (such as `*_windows.go`) and exclude `*_test.go` files. Do not list `MatchItem` itself.
tasks.rationale: Computed as all callers up to 3 levels up the gotool edges (static edges, union of GOOS darwin, linux and windows) call graph; 17 functions. Each item's note gives its level and the function it calls on the way to the target. Cross-checked with type-checked uses (gotool refs) of every level-1 and level-2 function: no use outside the set.

tasks.question: Which functions or methods call `decodeBase64` (src/utils/encode.ts) directly, or call one of its direct callers (two levels up the call chain)? Calls through callback parameters, interface-typed values or function values do not count. Only non-test files under `src/` (exclude `*.test.ts` and `*.test.tsx`). Do not list `decodeBase64` itself.
tasks.rationale: Computed as all callers up to 2 levels up the ts_edges.js (type-checker resolved, `direct` edges) call graph; 13 functions. Each item's note gives its level and the function it calls on the way to the target. `handle` is the AWS Lambda adapter's (the Lambda@Edge `handle` is three levels up).

tasks.question: Which test files under src/ (`*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`) exercise `bufferToFormData` (src/utils/buffer.ts) through a chain of direct calls: code in the test file calls it, or calls a non-test function from which it is reachable through direct calls? Code anywhere in a test file counts, including inside `describe`/`it` callbacks and handlers the file defines. Count only direct calls (`new` included) that resolve to a declaration, following imports, re-exports and the static type of the receiver (so `c.req.parseBody()` calls `HonoRequest.parseBody`), whatever the arguments or branches; inside non-test code, a call in a nested function or callback counts for the outermost named function that contains it. Calls through callback parameters, interface-typed values or function values do not count, and sending a request to an app (`app.request(...)`, `fetch`) does not count as calling its handlers. Answer with file paths.
tasks.rationale: The test files among all transitive callers in the ts_edges.js (type-checker resolved, `direct` edges, test files included); 10 files. Chains run through validator, HonoRequest.parseBody, parseBody, parseFormData and methodOverride.

tasks.question: FastAPI defines its own `HTTPException` class in fastapi/exceptions.py, a subclass of Starlette's class of the same name, and modules of the package import one or the other. Which functions or methods in the `fastapi/` package construct an instance of FastAPI's `HTTPException` (fastapi/exceptions.py) - not Starlette's - either directly or by calling a method that constructs one? A call through `self` runs the implementation that the instance's class uses (inherited unless overridden). Ignore docstrings and comments.
tasks.rationale: Only fastapi/security/http.py and fastapi/security/oauth2.py import fastapi.exceptions.HTTPException; routing.py, api_key.py, open_id_connect_url.py and telemetry/_api.py construct Starlette's. The two make_not_authenticated_error methods construct it (level 1); every __call__ that runs one of them through self, inherited and not overridden, is level 2; 9 methods. Derived with py_edges.py and checked by reading every `HTTPException(` and `make_not_authenticated_error(` site in fastapi/.
